decisions.reason: The source clarifies the power-chain relationship among existing boards but does not change the candidate's board count, separate-board architecture, or board inventory.
The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY recording the INA219 position and combined downstream 3.3V measurement coverage; no additional update or removal is required.
The interboard power-chain clarification does not alter battery-connector placement, connector orientation, mounting-hole clearance, or physical accessibility.
The source does not change the power board's four-layer stack.
The power-routing clarification does not change enclosure fit, dimensions, aspect ratio, USB-C placement, or mounting requirements.
The source does not modify the charge-status display method, external charge LED circuit, connector, resistance, or component population.
The source describes normal interboard power distribution and INA219 placement but does not change standalone USB activation, LDO selection, Schottky OR-ing, or the USB-powered 3.3V load set.
The referenced interboard cable carries power in this decision; no I2C cable length, pull-up, bus-speed, series-resistor, or signal-topology rule changes.
The source clarifies 3.3V distribution and monitoring, not the LEDs' 5V supply, level shifting, GPIO, or standby power control.
The main board's role in forwarding power does not alter the panel-control connector inventory, GPIO assignments, or onboard-button policy.
Receiving forwarded power does not change the sensor board's independently defined role as a connector fanout for external sensors.

The existing state already defines DCDC1 as the normal 3.3V source for the main-board and downstream sensor loads; the source adds routing and metering detail without changing voltage, rating, or regulation role.
